title: Mixed Interview Set: Unlabeled Problems Against the Clock
oneLiner: Random problems from the graded lessons with the titles and hints stripped off, on an interview timer.
keyTakeaway: Every lesson tells you its pattern in the title before you start, which is exactly the part an interview doesn't give you. Practising on unlabeled problems against a clock is the closest thing to the real round: read, name the approach out loud, code it, test it, and keep an eye on the time.
explanation:
Pick a format and the set draws problems at random from the Patterns, Graphs and Dynamic Programming lessons. You see a plain problem statement and a couple of examples, nothing else: no title, no explanation, no visualizer, no TODO hints in the starter code and no reference solution.

Before the editor opens you commit to a technique, the same way an interviewer expects you to explain your approach before writing code. Then solve it against the lesson's real tests. A pass counts toward that lesson's progress like any other. When you pass, or give up, the set tells you which lesson it was and whether your call matched, and the summary at the end links to each lesson so you can study the ones that got away.

The clock keeps running past zero, because finishing slowly still teaches you more than stopping, but the summary records how far over you went. Problems you drew recently are less likely to come up again.
